title: GOOD: Rate limiter keys by IP not IP:port, preventing N-connection burst
description: peering/session.rs deliberately extracts the IP address (peer_ip) separate from the full socket address (peer_addr), and uses peer_ip as the rate limiter key. The comment explicitly states the rationale: multiple simultaneous connections from one host share a single rate budget, preventing N-connection burst multiplication. This is the correct design — keying by IP:port would allow a peer to multiply its effective rate limit by opening N connections. The design is also applied consistently to blacklist checks (is_blacklisted and check_and_blacklist both use peer_ip).
